title: What Scripture says of the Father and the Son it says of the Spirit
english: …the Word, or they will be seen to act against the Scriptures.

For nothing is ranked with the Trinity in one Godhead: not the spirits because they are called spirits, to say nothing of the profane ones; not human beings because they are called gods, for we are not gods in truth. And if they do not think that the words “to the only wise God” (Romans 16:27) and “who alone has immortality” (1 Timothy 6:16) tell against themselves, they will not be able to use anything at all to argue cleverly against the Holy Spirit. For Paul spoke in this way because the Son is the Word of God and the Holy Spirit is his Spirit, and they belong to him inseparably by nature and are referred back to one Godhead. Even among those outside it is said: “One God, self-fathered, from whom all these things came to be.”

As Paul, then, wrote of the Father to the Romans, the Galatians and Timothy, “God is one” (Romans 3:30; Galatians 3:20; 1 Timothy 2:5), so John said of the Son, “the only-begotten God, who is in the bosom of the Father” (John 1:18); and of the Holy Spirit Paul taught the Corinthians, “to another gifts of healing in the one Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:9). For oneness is proper to the divine nature, which is not multiplied. And as it was written that the Son was begotten, and he says in witness, “I came forth from the Father” (John 16:28), so it was written, and the same Lord said, “the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father” (John 15:26), that is, who proceeded.

And as the Son, being God and Lord, is the Son of God and Lord, so the Holy Spirit, being God and Lord, is the Spirit of God and Lord. And as the Son is written “Word” because he exists together with the Father, in the same way the Holy Spirit is written “utterance of God” (Ephesians 6:17), and “breath of his mouth” (Psalm 33:6), and “breath of the Almighty” (Job 33:4), since, subsisting together with him, he shone forth from him; so that no one may suppose him to be outside the Godhead of the Father or of his Word. For the utterance belongs to the word, and the word to the mind; and so the saying is fulfilled, “the one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all” (Ephesians 4:6).

And as the Son is shown to be indistinguishable from the Father where it is written, “He who has seen me has seen the Father” (John 14:9), so is the Holy Spirit, by the words, “By this we know that God is in us, by his Spirit whom he has given us” (1 John 3:24). It is altogether necessary, then, since the Father is true God, that he too who shows him by his own manifestation should be true God, equal to him.

And as all things came to be through the Son (John 1:3), so by the Spirit all things were sanctified and empowered. For the apostles say: “Master, you who made heaven and earth and the sea and all that is in them, who through the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of David your servant, [said]” (Acts 4:24–25). And as the Only-begotten is shown to be equal in power with the Father, like him, and sovereign, according to the words, “Whatever the Father does, these things the Son also does likewise” (John 5:19), so too is the Spirit of God, according to the words, “All these things the one and the same Spirit works” (1 Corinthians 12:11).

And as Christ said of himself, “No one has known the Father except the Son” (Matthew 11:27), so the like is said of the Holy Spirit: “No one has known the things of God except the Spirit of God” (1 Corinthians 2:11). And as the Son, because he announces, was called “Messenger of great counsel” (Isaiah 9:5 LXX), so it is with the Holy Spirit too, for Scripture says: “But we received the Spirit of God, that we might know the things freely given to us by God” (1 Corinthians 2:12).

Very like “Christ the firstfruits” (1 Corinthians 15:23) is the text that says, “and having the firstfruits of the Spirit” (Romans 8:23). Matched with “May the Lord sanctify you, that you may be pure and blameless for the day of redemption” is “that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable, sanctified in the Holy Spirit” (Romans 15:16). And of equal weight with saying, “He who set me apart from my mother’s womb, through his grace, to reveal his Christ in me” (Galatians 1:15–16), is “God revealed it through his Spirit” (1 Corinthians 2:10).

Of equal force with saying, “Examine yourselves, whether Christ is in you” (2 Corinthians 13:5), is the saying, “We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit of God” (1 Corinthians 2:12). And “Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you?” (1 Corinthians 3:16) is equal to what John wrote, “If we love one another, God abides in us. By this we know that we abide in him and he in us, by his Spirit whom he has given us” (1 John 4:12–13), and to “I and the Father will come and make our dwelling with him” (John 14:23).

And as the Holy Spirit is given through the Father and the Son, according to “I will pour out of my Spirit on all flesh” (Joel 2:28) and according to “Receive the Holy Spirit” (John 20:22), so through the Holy Spirit Christ is given, according to Paul, who writes to the Ephesians, “that he may grant you …

part of the same conflated quotation in 5.15 (“that you may be pure and blameless”)

The old English printed edition numbers 5.13-5.17 in the reading text (reader report), broke 5.12 off mid-sentence ('a true God be equal to him and—'), made the Son 'distinct from' the Father (ἀπαράλλακτος, indistinguishable), turned 'oneness is proper to the divine, unmultiplied nature' into 'the plurality of nature', and garbled 5.9 ('the Trinity is not composed of something', 'made wise by anything from the opposite'). title: The Spirit speaks, sends and works as the Lord does
english: …according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his Spirit, so that Christ may dwell in the inner man” (Ephesians 3:16–17).

We may take as alike and equal “The word of the Lord came to such and such a prophet,” and “The Lord said,” and “Thus says the Lord Almighty,” with what Peter said in the Acts, “The Scripture had to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand” (Acts 1:16); with what Paul said in Rome to the Jews, “Well did the Holy Spirit speak through Isaiah the prophet” (Acts 28:25); and with “But the Spirit expressly says” (1 Timothy 4:1), and “Thus says the Lord Almighty.”

Of equal honour with “the eternal God” is what Paul proclaimed: “who offered himself through the eternal Spirit” (Hebrews 9:14). Comparable with “No one can receive the Holy Spirit except from the Lord,” and with “Receive the Holy Spirit” (John 20:22), is “No one can say ‘Lord Jesus Christ’ except in the Holy Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:3).

To be “guided by the Holy Spirit into the truth” (John 16:13), that is, to be guided by the Holy Spirit into the true faith, is the same as to be guided by the Master Christ when he decrees, “baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19). Of equal strength with the text that says, “Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?” (1 Corinthians 10:22), is the writing, “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption” (Ephesians 4:30). And worded alike with “You will send forth your Spirit, and they will be created” (Psalm 104:30) is “You will send forth your word, and it will melt them” (Psalm 147:18).

On a par with saying, “The Lord bears witness to my soul that I do not lie,” is the writing, “The Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness about me” (John 15:26), and “The Spirit bears witness to me in every city, saying” (Acts 20:23). And likened to the Master’s saying, “Behold, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves” (Matthew 10:16), is “So these, sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia” (Acts 13:4).

The writing “Since you seek proof of the Christ who speaks in me” (2 Corinthians 13:3) is equal to the writing that “they told Paul through the Spirit, Do not go up to Jerusalem” (Acts 21:4). Akin to “The Son is eternal life” is what he himself said: “The water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water leaping up to eternal life” (John 4:14). “Now this he said about the Holy Spirit, whom those who believed in him were to receive” (John 7:39). And akin to “For we have become partakers of Christ” (Hebrews 3:14) is “For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and become partakers of the Holy Spirit” (Hebrews 6:4).

What is said in the Acts in these words, “There appeared to the apostles tongues as of fire, divided, and they sat on each one of them, and all were filled with the Holy Spirit” (Acts 2:3–4), and what John said, “He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire” (Matthew 3:11), are very like what was declared by Moses, “God is a consuming fire” (Deuteronomy 4:24), and by Isaiah, “Behold, the Lord will come as fire” (Isaiah 66:15). And the saying “You were circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, in putting off the body of sins, in the circumcision of Christ” (Colossians 2:11) is in harmony with the written words “circumcision of the heart, in the Spirit” (Romans 2:29).

And if Peter’s words are fitly said about God, “Let each one repent of his wickedness and of the evil way, and be baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus, and he will be saved” (Acts 2:38), then his Spirit is indistinguishable from God. This is plain also from the Master’s words to the disciples, in so many words: “Wait for the promise of the Father, which you have heard, that John baptized with water for repentance, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit” (Acts 1:4–5). For this shows nothing other than what his other teaching on the rite of enlightenment shows: that the Holy Spirit works and is able to do the very things that the name of the Father and of his Son does, since he is of the same Godhead.

The preaching of the Son and that of the Holy Spirit are without difference and equally to be revered, as Paul writes to the Romans: “For if he who comes preaches another Jesus, whom we did not preach, or you receive a different spirit, which you did not receive” (2 Corinthians 11:4). The same proof lies in “For I will not dare to speak of anything except what Christ has worked through me to bring the Gentiles to obedience, by word and deed, in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Spirit of God” (Romans 15:18–19), as in “The Father who abides in me does the works himself. Believe that I am in the Father and the Father in me” (John 14:10–11). For observe that, as the Father, so too the …

title: The one Spirit, the utterance of God, is no creature
english: …his Spirit abides with Christ, being inseparable in the divine nature; and that the divine works are done by the ineffable Trinity with one mind; and that, as the Father, existing in his own hypostasis, is imaged in the Only-begotten because their Godhead, that is, their essence, is without difference, in the same way the Only-begotten is imaged in the one Holy Spirit. And how many other things are set down about the divine Spirit that do not differ from what is written about God the Father and his only-begotten Son! Some of them are contained in various places of this book, through which the course of the argument has passed.

Besides, when they are questioned in turn, will they not say that Eve, and the children born of her, came from Adam? How then were the children written as begotten, while she was called neither his child nor the sister of those who were born? Yet the single and incomparable nature cannot be shown by a comparison drawn from creatures, since it remains unseen by the mind and does not allow itself even to be brought forth to the hearing or in words. For even if some small shadow of a likeness, so to speak, is found in some way, the greater part escapes and leaves the one who draws the comparison somewhere far below. An example can never be identity. It is safe to say only those things which the Scriptures have taught, to the measure of our capacity.

That the Spirit of God the Father is written to be one and only, because he is separated by nature from the other spirits and joined to the Father and his Son in the very account of essence, Paul teaches. He writes to the Corinthians in the first letter: “to another gifts of healing in the one Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:9); and again: “All these things the one and the same Spirit works, dividing to each one individually as he wills” (1 Corinthians 12:11); and again: “We were all made to drink of one Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:13). To the Ephesians he writes: “for through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father” (Ephesians 2:18); and again: “eager to keep the unity of the Spirit” (Ephesians 4:3), that is, to take great care not to separate him from the supreme Unity and self-complete essence.

That he is also named “utterance,” they bear witness in this way. Paul writes to the Ephesians: “Taking up the whole armour of God, and the breastplate of righteousness, and the shield of faith, and the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the utterance of God” (Ephesians 6:13–17). Matthew too mentioned this sword, speaking in the person of Christ: “I did not come to bring peace, but a sword” (Matthew 10:34). He does not mean a blade, but the indescribable wisdom of the Holy Spirit, which reaches beyond peace and cuts through hardened hearts. And Paul writes to the Hebrews: “upholding all things by the utterance of his power” (Hebrews 1:3).

By what utterance? David prophesied: “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the Spirit of his mouth all their powers” (Psalm 33:6). And again Paul: “For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and become partakers of the Holy Spirit, and have tasted the good utterance of God” (Hebrews 6:4–5). And Peter: “For all flesh is as grass, and all its glory as the flower of grass. The grass withered and the flower fell, and its beauty perished; but the utterance of God abides for ever” (1 Peter 1:24–25). In the same way the Psalmist sings of the Son in the hundred and nineteenth Psalm: “For ever, O Lord, your word abides in heaven” (Psalm 119:89). For Scripture hands down many things, in a most hidden way, about the highest and most divine hypostases.
That everything proper to the Godhead is attested of the Holy Spirit, as follows.

Next, then, the Scriptures declare about the pure and inexpressible nature of the Holy Spirit such things as they declare about God the Father, who holds sway over all, and about the Son, who is beyond all and Lord of all, because he is not of another essence, nor less in power and glory. And none of these things is found to belong of itself to any created thing. For whatever a creature does have, it has as a gift bestowed by the Trinity in one Godhead. And each thing can always be recognized from what belongs to it: what it is and what it is not, whether it is God by nature or a creature. For example:
That he is not the first creature, as the heretics say, but God.

For the first creature is Satan. Creation has being, though at first it was not; and it was shown in Job which is the first thing made among rational beings, for the book speaks of the devil, who belied his nature by his conduct. But that the Holy Spirit, as “breath of the Almighty” (Job 33:4), is a creature or has any beginning at all is nowhere written. For no thing made could have existed before the Spirit who makes, and such a …
